subject: Fraud & Scams
title: How Stock Manipulation Works
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How Stock Manipulation Works.

hook.text: Buying millions of shares raises a stock price. Selling them all at once crashes it. Both can be fraud.

buildup.text: Stock manipulation distorts prices so that insiders profit at the expense of regular investors.

discovery.text: Techniques include wash trading, spoofing, and coordinating purchases in chat rooms.

twist.text: High-frequency trading makes manipulation harder to detect — and faster to execute.

climax.text: The SEC investigates hundreds of manipulation cases yearly but can only pursue a fraction.

punchline.text: The market is fair — until someone with enough money decides it isn't.

quiz.question: What is 'spoofing' in stock manipulation?
options: Buying stocks under a fake name
Placing fake orders to move prices, then canceling them
